transcript: Every year, about 8 million tons of plastic flow into the world's oceans That equals one truckload every minute in the Pacific Ocean A huge area of garbage twice the size of Texas is floating Called the Great Pacific Garbage Patch Debris carried by the currents has gathered there over many years Larger pieces of plastic Broken down by waves and ultraviolet light Slowly becomes microplastic These tiny particles enter the food chain From plankton to fish and eventually onto our dinner tables The impact on marine life is severe Whales and seabirds have mistaken plastic bags for food wouldn't have died after swallowing them. Coral reefs, too, face the double threat of chemical pollution and warming waters. Governments around the world have introduced various policies, such as charging for plastic bags and banning certain plastics. Companies, on the other hand, have invested in biodegradable materials And recycling technology In the end, the problem will be solved by the choices each of us makes Reduce, reuse, recycle So the accumulation of small choices in daily life will change the future of the ocean
